title: 2023 HMMT February Team Problem 9
statement: Let \(A B C\) be a triangle with \(A B<A C\). The incircle of triangle \(A B C\) is tangent to side \(B C\) at \(D\) and intersects the perpendicular bisector of segment \(B C\) at distinct points \(X\) and \(Y\). Lines \(A X\) and \(A Y\) intersect line \(B C\) at \(P\) and \(Q\), respectively. Prove that, if \(D P \cdot D Q=(A C-A B)^{2}\), then \(A B+A C=3 B C\).

solutions.text: Solution: Let \(E\) be the extouch point on \(B C\), let \(I\) be the incenter, and \(D^{\prime}\) the reflection of \(D\) over \(I\). Note that \(D E=A C-A B\), so \(D P \cdot D Q=D E^{2}\). Now let \(F\) be the reflection of \(E\) across \(D\). The length condition implies \((E, F ; P, Q)\) is a harmonic bundle. We also know \(X Y\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(D E\), so the midpoint \(M\) of \(D^{\prime} E\) lies on \(X Y\). But then \(I M \| B C\), so \(I M \perp X Y\), and \(M\) is the midpoint of \(X Y\). Since \(A, D^{\prime}, E\) are collinear, this means \(A E\) bisects \(X Y\). Now consider projecting \((E, F ; P, Q)\) onto \(X Y . P\) and \(Q\) are taken to \(X\) and \(Y\), while \(E\) is taken to the midpoint of \(X Y\). Thus, \(F\) is taken to the point at infinity, so \(A F \perp B C\). Now since \(D\) is the midpoint of \(E F\), we see that \(A F=2 D D^{\prime}\), or \(h_{a}=2 r\), where \(h_{a}\) is the height from \(A\) and \(r\) is the inradius. But \(\frac{1}{2} a h_{a}=\frac{a+b+c}{2} r\), so \(a=\frac{a+b+c}{2}\), or \(3 a=b+c\), as desired.
